subject: Maths
title: Proportion graphs
subtitle: Proportion · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can interpret and draw graphs showing direct and inverse proportion.

key_vocab.definition: A direct proportion graph is a straight line through the origin. An inverse proportion graph is a curve (hyperbola) that never touches the axes.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can interpret and draw graphs showing direct and inverse proportion.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: Proportion graphs -- A direct proportion graph is a straight line through the origin. An inverse proportion graph is a curve (hyperbola) that never touches the axes.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Direct proportion: straight line through origin (gradient = k). Inverse proportion: reciprocal curve.
Direct: y = kx | Inverse: y = &frac{k}{x}
Recognise the shape to identify the type

Key examples:
  ✓ Direct proportion: straight line through (0, 0)  (y = kx)
  ✓ Inverse proportion: curve approaching axes  (y = k/x)
  ✓ Gradient of direct proportion line = k  (constant rate)
  ✗ Any straight line shows direct proportion  (must pass through origin)
  ✗ Inverse proportion graphs are straight lines  (they are curves)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – direct proportion graph
  The graph of y against x passes through (0, 0) and (4, 12). Is this direct proportion? Find k.
  Passes through origin: yes, could be direct proportion
  k = y/x = 12/4 = 3
  y = 3x
  Yes, k = 3
  (A straight line through the origin confirms direct proportion.)

Example 2 – reading values from a graph
  A direct proportion graph passes through (5, 20). Find y when x = 8.
  k = 20/5 = 4
  y = 4x
  When x = 8: y = 32
  y = 32
  (Use any point on the line to find k.)

sections.title: Identifying direct proportion
sections.content:
Does each graph show direct proportion? Explain.

(a) Straight line through (0,0) and (3,9)
(b) Straight line through (0,2) and (4,10)
(c) Curve through (1,6), (2,3), (3,2)
(d) Straight line through (0,0) and (5,15)

sections.title: Finding equations from graphs
sections.content:
Find the equation of proportion from the given point.

(a) Direct: passes through (4, 20)
(b) Direct: passes through (3, 7.5)
(c) Inverse: passes through (2, 10)
(d) Inverse: passes through (5, 4)

sections.title: Using proportion graphs
sections.content:
Use the given equation to find missing values.

(a) y = 4x. Find y when x = 7
(b) y = 4x. Find x when y = 30
(c) y = 24/x. Find y when x = 3
(d) y = 24/x. Find x when y = 2

sections.title: Real-world proportion graphs
sections.content:
Identify the type and solve.

(a) Cost vs quantity (straight line through origin). k = 2.50. Cost of 7 items?
(b) Speed vs time for fixed distance. At 30 mph, takes 4 hours. Time at 50 mph?
(c) Distance vs time at constant speed. Through (2, 100). Distance at t = 5?
(d) Workers vs days (curve). 4 workers, 10 days. Days for 8 workers?

sections.title: Mixed proportion graphs
sections.content:
Classify and calculate.

(a) y and x: (1,5), (2,10), (3,15). Type and equation?
(b) y and x: (1,12), (2,6), (3,4). Type and equation?
(c) y = 3x. What does the graph look like?
(d) y = 8/x. What does the graph look like?
(e) A line through origin has gradient 7. Write the proportion equation.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ Direct proportion graphs pass through the origin
✗ Any straight line graph shows direct proportion
✓ Inverse proportion graphs are curves that approach the axes
✗ Inverse proportion graphs cross both axes
✓ The gradient of y = kx tells you k

  (b) y = 2.5x
  (c) y = 20/x
  (d) y = 20/x

Using proportion graphs:
  (a) 28
  (b) 7.5
  (c) 8
  (d) 12

Real-world proportion graphs:
  (a) £17.50
  (b) 2.4 hours
  (c) 250 km
  (d) 5 days

Mixed proportion graphs:
